question: Consider two equivalence relations $R_1$ and $R_2$ on a finite set $A$. Prove that $R = R_1 \cap R_2$ is also an equivalence relation on $A$.

options.A: $R_1 \cap R_2$ is not an equivalence relation because intersection destroys reflexivity
options.B: $R_1 \cap R_2$ is not an equivalence relation because it is symmetric only
options.C: $R_1 \cap R_2$ is an equivalence relation because it is reflexive, symmetric and transitive
options.D: $R_1 \cap R_2$ is a universal relation for every finite set $A$
